title: Stop confirming orders the shop can't fill

blocks.text: The shop's checkout runs one consumer for every order it accepts. That consumer takes the stock, emails the customer, and, where the deployment has one, writes the order to a compliance log. Support has two complaints: customers get "your order is on its way" for orders that were then refused because the warehouse was out of stock, and the staging deployment, which has no compliance log, can't be started with the current code.
Write `build(reserve, confirm, audit)` in `src/main/java/practice/OrderPipeline.java`. The steps are given to you; you decide how they are put together. When you're done:

items: a customer is emailed only about an order whose stock was reserved;
when the stock can't be reserved, the checkout gets that exception as it was thrown, so it can show the customer why;
the compliance log holds only orders whose customer was emailed;
a deployment that passes `null` for `audit` still takes orders.

cases.says: an order that is in stock is reserved, confirmed and audited once each
no confirmation is emailed for an order whose stock could not be reserved
the exception that refused the reservation reaches the checkout unchanged
with no compliance log configured, orders are still reserved and confirmed
an order whose confirmation email failed is not written to the compliance log

origin.section: andThen Runs the Steps in Order, and Stops at the First One That Throws

concepts: a.andThen(b) runs a, then b, on the same value, and if a throws, b does not run and the exception reaches the caller; so the step that can refuse goes first and the irreversible one last.
andThen(null) throws NullPointerException when the chain is built, not when it runs, so an optional step needs an explicit choice.
